questions.question: What is an environmental pollutant?
choices: Any naturally occurring substance regardless of amount
A substance or energy input capable of environmental harm
Only human-made materials that are visibly colored
Any environmental change that benefits all organisms

questions.question: What is a point source of pollution?
choices: Pollution spread across many diffuse sources
Any source that is impossible to locate
Only a source on a mountain
A specific identifiable discharge location

questions.question: What is nonpoint-source pollution?
choices: Pollution arising from diffuse sources such as runoff across land
Pollution from one identifiable discharge pipe only
Only pollutants that cannot dissolve in water
Only air pollution emitted from one factory stack

questions.question: What is bioaccumulation?
choices: The increase of a pollutant across successive food-chain levels
The decrease of concentration through dilution
The buildup of a substance in an organism over time
The transport of a substance out of every organism

questions.question: What is biomagnification?
choices: An organism's pollutant buildup throughout its own lifetime
A decline in pollutant concentration at higher trophic levels
The equal distribution of every pollutant among food-chain levels
Increasing concentrations of some pollutants at higher trophic levels

questions.question: What is eutrophication?
choices: The removal of nutrients from a water body
Only a temperature increase without nutrient enrichment
Nutrient enrichment that can stimulate excessive aquatic growth
Only the buildup of salt in seawater

questions.question: What is thermal pollution?
choices: A harmful alteration of environmental temperature, often in receiving water
Only a natural seasonal change with no harmful input
The buildup of dissolved nutrients alone
The introduction of solid waste regardless of temperature

questions.question: Why can excessive nutrient runoff reduce oxygen in a lake?
choices: Nutrients directly remove all oxygen without biological processes
Decomposition of increased organic matter can consume dissolved oxygen
Algae never produce oxygen under any conditions
Decomposition cannot consume dissolved oxygen

questions.question: Why can persistent pollutants remain a concern after discharge stops?
choices: Pollutants must vanish as soon as their source closes
Persistent means the substance cannot move between places
Persistence proves there is no future exposure
They may break down slowly and remain in the environment

questions.question: Why does pollution risk depend on both hazard and exposure?
choices: Only the substance's name determines risk
Potential harm and the amount of contact both matter
All detectable amounts cause identical effects
Contact duration and amount have no effect on potential harm

questions.question: Why can preventing pollution at its source be useful?
choices: Source prevention guarantees immediate ecosystem recovery
Source prevention makes pollution monitoring unnecessary
It reduces the amount needing later treatment or cleanup
Cleanup is always more effective than reducing releases

questions.question: Why can sediment runoff harm an aquatic habitat?
choices: It can reduce light and cover sensitive habitats
Sediment always improves light penetration
Sediment affects only rivers with no organisms
Only dissolved pollutants can alter aquatic habitats

questions.question: Why is noise considered pollution in some settings?
choices: Excessive sound can disrupt organisms and communication
All sound causes identical environmental harm
Sound cannot affect animal behavior
Only chemical substances can be considered pollution

questions.question: Why can pollution move beyond its source area?
choices: Every pollutant remains permanently where it is released
Air transports pollutants but water never can
Air and water can transport pollutants
Pollutants move only inside animals

questions.question: Why is a single clear-water observation insufficient to rule out pollution?
choices: Clear water contains no dissolved substances
Some contaminants are dissolved or otherwise invisible
All contamination has a strong odor
Water color identifies every pollutant present

questions.question: Which example best represents nonpoint-source pollution?
choices: Wastewater leaving one identified discharge pipe
Smoke leaving one factory stack
A leak from one identified storage tank
Rain washing fertilizer from many lawns into streams

questions.question: A persistent pollutant has 1 unit of concentration in prey and 10 units in their predators. What pattern does this illustrate?
choices: Dilution
Evaporation
Biomagnification
Radioactive dating

questions.question: A lake experiences an algal bloom followed by lower dissolved oxygen as algae decay. Which mechanism fits?
choices: Decomposers consume oxygen while breaking down organic matter
All oxygen becomes nitrogen instantly
Dead algae no longer interact with the environment
The lake must have become colder

questions.question: An investigation compares pollution upstream and downstream of a discharge point. Why sample both?
choices: Upstream water must contain no pollutants
Downstream water never mixes
One location automatically proves the cause
The upstream site helps provide a comparison condition

questions.question: A cleanup removes surface litter but dissolved pollutants remain. What conclusion follows?
choices: Removing litter guarantees removal of dissolved chemicals
Different forms of pollution may require different responses
Dissolved contaminants cannot be detected
The remaining water is safe for every use
